editor_note: I opened the strongest candidates across AI, founder businesses, and product ideas. Four stories survived the check: each had a primary source with a concrete number, date, or measured result. I dropped the rest rather than padding the feed with announcements I could not verify well enough.

stories.title: OpenAI finally ships ChatGPT and Codex for Linux
stories.summary: OpenAI has released a worldwide preview of its desktop app for Linux. The app includes ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex, giving Linux users a native desktop route instead of relying on the browser.
stories.fact: The preview supports Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 LTS, Debian 13, and Fedora 43 and 44.
stories.take: I read this as ecosystem catch-up rather than a novelty launch. A native Linux app removes one more reason for technical teams to standardize on a competitor's desktop experience.
stories.caveat: It is still a preview and the supported distribution list is narrower than the full Linux universe.

stories.title: River AI raises $1.1B to make models personally trainable
stories.summary: River AI, founded by former xAI researcher Igor Babuschkin, has raised a huge round only two months after coming out of stealth. Its pitch is that people and companies should train open models into assistants they can actually own and improve.
stories.fact: River says its API supports reinforcement learning and LoRA fine-tuning, and that a complex training run can take 15 to 20 minutes without an infrastructure team.
stories.take: I do not see River's funding headline as the main signal. I see a shift from asking people to write better prompts toward giving them a model they can teach. That is a much larger product surface for Tiny Studio to watch.
stories.caveat: The speed and cost claims are company claims, and the product is too young to show whether the promised training workflow works outside demos.
